2.  25-57002  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation on Continuum of Care (CoC)
  Program Funding Updates from the Health Department.

  Page 1 of 6
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 18, 2025
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 3:00 PM

A motion was made by Member Amick, seconded by Member Martins, to
approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

Yes:  9 Amick, Brown-Shock, Diles III, Martins, McFadzen, Topolewski,
  Shuford, Wee, Scott
No:  0 None
Recused: 0 None
Abstain: 0 None
Absent: 6 Boyce, Brezenoff, Lock, Rockenbach, Tan, Lowery-Luyties

  • Health Department staff Joseph Botelho provided an overview and
  discussed strategies to respond to the CoC program NOFO.
  • FY 2025 NOFO released November 13, 2025, there is approximately $3.918
  billion in funding available.
  • HUD has substantially reshaped the competition, Tier 1 is 30% of the CoC’s
  annual renewal demand and permanent housing projects are capped at
  30% of CoC’s ARD.
  • Scoring factors have shifted away from local competition mechanics and
  refocused on demonstrated reductions in unsheltered homelessness,
  reallocation and the composition and participation of the CoC’s governance
  structure.
  • New policy priorities include: focus of resources on outreach, intervention,
  and assistance consistent with Executive order 14321 Ending Crime and
  Disorder on American Streets.
  • CoC’s now expected to prioritize projects that provide treatment and service
  participation requirements.
  • CoC’s directed to cooperate with law enforcement to advance public safety.
  • CoC’s should prioritize long-term economic independence, self sufficiency
  and support treatment and recovery.
  • Projects could be reduced /rejected if previously or currently conduct
  activities that use a definition of sex other than as binary in humans.
  • Board member Topolewski asked about the intended outcome with the shift
  to transitional housing. Staff responded.
  • This NOFO highlights housing affordability as short term and not long term.
  • Member McFadzen had a question regarding the minutes, staff clarified the
  question.
  • Staff discussed the changes to the application scoring and reviewed the LB
  CoC projects and individuals that are currently funded.
  • Long Beach CoC’s Strategic Response inlcudes policy language to preserve
  local priorities, scoring and ranking policies, reallocation policy and funding
  priorities. Staff anticipate a Special Board meeting during the first two weeks
  of December.
  • Members of the board had questions about the steps the other CoC’s are
  taking, staff responded.

3.  25-57003  Recommendation to review and approve the Long Beach Continuum of Care
  (CoC) Scoring and Ranking Policies.

  A motion was made by Member Brown-Shock, seconded by Member
  McFadzen, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  9 Amick, Brown-Shock, Diles III, Martins, McFadzen, Topolewski,
  Shuford, Wee, Scott
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 6 Boyce, Brezenoff, Lock, Rockenbach, Tan, Lowery-Luyties

  • Health Department staff Joseph Botelho provided an overview of the updates
  to the Scoring and Ranking Policies. HUD requires CoCs to review, assess,
  and score project applications for performance as part of the CoC Program
  Competition.
  • HUD is now requiring at least 50% of scoring points be based on objective
  criteria defining, including cost effectiveness, performance data, and
  populations served. An additional 25% of points must be tied to system
  performance measures, specifically returns to homelessness and
  employment income. Participation requirements are included within this 25%
  category.
  • Minor revisions to ranking exemptions. Long Beach prioritizes permanent
  supportive housing and acknowledges the NOFO requirements may require
  adjustments to competitive scoring and ranking criteria to maximize
  competitiveness and preserve funding.
  • These adjustments are made in response to the NOFO requirements and do
  not represent any change in the community’s local prioritization of permanent
  housing.
  • Additionally, contingency language for scoring and ranking was reviewed
  with the board.
  • Members of the board and staff discussed changes that HUD is making
  along with the funding that will be received.
  • A member of the public commented regarding the transitions that are being
  made, they suggested reaching out to providers to see who would like to
  make these shifts collectively.

4.  25-57004  Recommendation to review and approve the Long Beach Continuum of Care
  (CoC) Reallocation Policies and Procedures.

  A motion was made by Member Martins, seconded by Co-Chair Diles III, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9 Amick, Brown-Shock, Diles III, Martins, McFadzen, Topolewski,
  Shuford, Wee, Scott
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 6 Boyce, Brezenoff, Lock, Rockenbach, Tan, Lowery-Luyties

  • Health Department Staff Joseph Botelho provided an update on the
  Reallocation Policies and Procedures, noting that HUD requires all CoCs to
  maintain a reallocation process as part of the CoC program competition. He
  explained that there are two types of reallocation involuntary and voluntary.
  • The City may use reallocation to preserve the overall CoC funding
  level. These adjustments are not a reflection of changes in local priorities but
  are made solely to ensure that CoC remains competitive and maintains its
  funding.
  • A member of the public expressed appreciation for the information provided.
  Other attendees asked questions regarding the application process and
  upcoming deadlines.

5.  25-57005  Recommendation to review and approve the Long Beach Continuum of Care
  (CoC) Funding Priorities Guidance.

  A motion was made by Member McFadzen, seconded by Member Brown-
  Shock, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  9 Amick, Brown-Shock, Diles III, Martins, McFadzen, Topolewski,
  Shuford, Wee, Scott
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 6 Boyce, Brezenoff, Lock, Rockenbach, Tan, Lowery-Luyties

  • Health Department staff member Joseph Botelho presented an overview of
  funding available to CA-606 through the FY 2025 CoC NOFO. Updates to
  the Funding Priorities Guidance include minor revisions to language and
  funding priorities.He noted that the Funding Priorities Guidance has been
  updated with minor language revisions and adjustments to priority areas.

  Page 4 of 6
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 18, 2025
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 3:00 PM

  Staff also indicated that the upcoming NOFO may require Long Beach to
  reallocate existing projects or submit new project proposals to remain
  competitive and maintain funding eligibility.
  • The discussion also reviewed current project types and their annual renewal
  demand. Once the NOFO is released, it will provide clearer guidance on
  eligible project types, funding caps, and policy priorities. The CoC reaffirmed
  that the development and preservation of Permanent Housing remain key
  priorities and that funding efforts will continue to focus on eligible permanent
  housing project types.
  • A board member and staff discussed how racial preferences and binary sex
  will be addressed.
  • A member of the public asked whether recalculating project amounts could
  help maintain the program; staff clarified that voluntary reallocation is an
  option.
  • Another member of the public inquired about the amount of funding Long
  Beach plans to apply for. Staff explained that they are not yet able to
  disclose that information but will share it once it becomes available.

6.  25-57015  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Count Presentation and
  Updates from the Health Department.

  A motion was made by Member Amick, seconded by Member Martins, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9 Amick, Brown-Shock, Diles III, Martins, McFadzen, Topolewski,
  Shuford, Wee, Scott
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 6 Boyce, Brezenoff, Lock, Rockenbach, Tan, Lowery-Luyties

  • Health Department staff Steven Perle provided an update on the Long Beach
  2026 Point-In Time Count that will take place on Thursday, January 22,
  2026. The goal is to be able to reach a total of 400 staff and volunteers.
  • The Count components will include unsheltered count, sheltered count,
  service-based access centers and youth count. The unsheltered count will
  be conducted on Wednesday, January 21, 2025.
  • All data collected will be conducted via the Survey123 app.
  • For those that are not able to volunteer, other ways to support include
  hygiene kit donations.
